watchdog_enabled.description: Enable or disable the watchdog functionality. When enabled, the system will reset if the watchdog is not periodically pinged.

device_path.description: Path to the AVR watchdog device node. Usually `/dev/avr_evtd` on Linkstation devices.

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum time (in seconds) without a watchdog ping before a hardware reset is triggered. Valid range: 1–255. Set to 0 to disable timer (not recommended).

heartbeat_seconds.description: Interval (in seconds) between watchdog pings. Must be less than `timeout_seconds` to prevent resets.

syslog_facility.description: Syslog facility to use when logging messages. Common options: `daemon`, `local0`–`local7`.

pre_ping_command.description: Optional shell command to execute before each watchdog ping (e.g., health check script). Should be lightweight and fast.

post_reset_command.description: Optional shell command to execute *after* a watchdog-triggered reset (e.g., cleanup, notification).

run_as_user.description: Unix username to run `avr_evtd` as. For security, consider using a dedicated non-root user.

run_as_group.description: Unix group name to run `avr_evtd` as.

monitored_files.description: List of files whose change should trigger a watchdog ping. Useful for detecting configuration reloads or critical file updates.

path.description: Absolute path to the file to monitor.

monitored_services.description: List of services to check periodically. If a service fails, the watchdog is pinged to keep the system alive until the service recovers.

name.description: Name of the service (must be manageable by `service` command).

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for service status check before considering it failed. Defaults to global `heartbeat_seconds` if omitted.

no_auto_restart.description: Disable automatic restart of `avr_evtd` if it crashes (for debugging). Leave disabled in production.
